meta.title: Wise Guard – threat catalog
meta.description: List of the most common fraud methods and threats, with warning signs and recommended actions. Relevant at any age — some methods target older people more often, others target younger, more online-native users.
meta.disclaimer: Educational material. In case of a real threat or suspected fraud, contact the police (997/112) or your bank.

threats.title: The "police officer / prosecutor" scam
threats.description: A scammer poses as a police officer or prosecutor, claims there is an investigation against a bank employee, and asks for your "help" by transferring or withdrawing money.
warning_signs: The caller pressures you to act urgently and secretly
Asks you not to tell your family
Gives you a number to call back — which belongs to them
advice: Hang up and call 112 or your local police station yourself
The police never ask for transfers or cash withdrawals
Always tell your family before making any financial decision

threats.title: The "grandchild / relative" scam
threats.description: Someone calls crying or with a changed voice, claiming to be your grandchild or child in an accident and urgently needing money.
warning_signs: The voice sounds different, excused as a cold
An urgent transfer or handover of cash to a courier is requested
They refuse a video call
advice: Call that person back on a number you already know to verify
Agree on a family safety password for such situations
Never hand over money under time pressure

threats.title: The "bank employee" scam
threats.description: A fake bank employee warns of an alleged fraud attempt on your account and tells you to install a remote-access app (e.g. AnyDesk, TeamViewer) or to give authorisation codes.
warning_signs: They ask you to install a remote-access program
They ask for an SMS code or online-banking login
The number appears to be your bank's number (spoofing)
advice: Hang up and call the number on your bank card or official bank website
Never install programs at a caller's request
Never give SMS codes, PINs or logins over the phone

threats.title: Fake winnings / phone lotteries
threats.description: You are told you won a competition you never entered, to extort a "collection fee" or card details.
warning_signs: A win without entering any competition
You must pay to collect the prize
Time pressure ("today only")
advice: Real prizes never require upfront payment
Hang up and ignore it
Do not give personal or card details

threats.title: "Yes / no" recordings (voice fraud)
threats.description: A scammer provokes a "yes" or "no" answer that is recorded and later used to confirm alleged financial obligations.
warning_signs: An unknown number asks strange, generic questions
The call is very short and formulaic
advice: Do not answer "yes"/"no" to unknown numbers — ask who is calling
If suspicious, hang up and report the number
Consider not answering unknown foreign numbers

threats.title: Fake blocked-account SMS (smishing)
threats.description: An SMS with a link claims your bank account is blocked or a parcel needs a surcharge, leading to a fake login page.
warning_signs: A link in an SMS from your "bank" or "courier"
Time pressure and threats of account blocking
The page address differs from the official one
advice: Do not tap links in SMS messages — type your bank's address yourself
Check parcel status on the courier's official site
Report suspicious SMS to CERT Polska at 8080

threats.title: BLIK code fraud
threats.description: Someone posing as a friend (often from a hijacked Facebook/Messenger account) asks for a BLIK code "for a moment", then withdraws cash or shops with your money.
warning_signs: A request for a BLIK code from an online "friend"
An unusual writing style of that person
An urgent, out-of-character money request
advice: Never share a BLIK code with anyone, even friends
Call your friend to verify the request
Report the hijacked account to the service administrators

threats.title: Fake transfer confirmations / bank phishing e-mail
threats.description: An e-mail looking like a bank message asks you to click a link and log in to "confirm" an operation.
warning_signs: The sender has a similar but not identical e-mail address
Language mistakes or unusual phrasing
The link leads to a page other than the bank
advice: Do not click links in suspicious e-mails
Always type the bank address yourself in the browser
If in doubt, call your bank

threats.title: Card skimming at ATMs
threats.description: A device placed on an ATM copies card data while a tiny camera watches the PIN being entered.
warning_signs: The ATM looks unusual or has extra parts at the reader
The PIN pad feels rough or does not fit
Someone stands very close while you enter the PIN
advice: Cover the keypad with your hand when entering the PIN
Use ATMs inside bank branches, well lit
Regularly check transaction history in the bank app

threats.title: Impersonating ZUS / tax office
threats.description: A message or call about arrears, a tax refund or a data update, asking for personal data or payment.
warning_signs: A request for personal data or account number by phone/e-mail
A link to an "official form" outside gov.pl
Threats of fines or arrest if you do not react
advice: Offices never ask for card data by phone or SMS
Verify by logging in yourself at gov.pl
If in doubt, call the relevant office

threats.title: Fake meter reader / inspector
threats.description: A person claiming to work for the gas, power or water company demands entry and payment for an "inspection" or "meter replacement".
warning_signs: No prior written notice of the visit
An immediate cash payment is demanded
Refusal to show an ID badge
advice: Always ask for ID and call the company to verify the visit
Real inspections are usually announced by letter
Do not let in people you cannot verify

threats.title: The "hot water / gas" doorstep repair scam
threats.description: Someone offers an "immediate" installation repair, roof painting or similar, demands upfront payment, then does the job badly or not at all.
warning_signs: An uninvited visit offering repairs "today, as I am in the area"
A demand for upfront cash payment
Pressure and intimidation with a high repair price
advice: Do not decide under pressure — ask for time to think
Consult family or a trusted tradesperson
Pay only after the work is done and checked

threats.title: Fake charity collector
threats.description: A person at the door or on the street collects "for a sick child" or another cause, often with no documentation.
warning_signs: No organisation ID or collection permit
Pushing for a quick cash donation
Cannot name the organisation or collection number
advice: Check the fundraiser online before donating
Donate by transfer to a verified account, not cash
Do not feel obliged to donate on the spot

threats.title: The "gas / water — entry and theft" method
threats.description: Two people: one distracts you (e.g. "checking the meter"), the other searches the home for money or valuables.
warning_signs: Two people, one asking you to show something in another room
A sudden, unarranged "official" visit
Distraction through conversation
advice: Do not let unknown people in without prior verification
Ask a neighbour or family member to be present
Keep valuables out of easy reach

threats.title: Fake courier surcharge
threats.description: An SMS or e-mail from a "courier company" demands a small surcharge for a parcel, leading to a fake payment page.
warning_signs: A payment link in an SMS
You never ordered any parcel
The page address differs from the courier's official site
advice: Check parcel status directly on the courier's site
Do not tap payment links in SMS messages
If in doubt, call the courier

threats.title: Fake "unpaid fine / arrears" letters
threats.description: A letter or e-mail about overdue payment with threats of legal consequences, demanding a quick payment to a given account.
warning_signs: Legal threats and time pressure
An unusual account number for payment
The sender cannot be verified
advice: Verify the case directly with the relevant office/court
Do not pay to the account in a suspicious letter
Consult family or a lawyer before paying

threats.title: Fake online shops / "too good to be true" offers
threats.description: A website or ad offers products at a very low price; after payment the goods never arrive.
warning_signs: A price much lower than anywhere else
Payment only by traditional transfer, no payment protection
No seller contact details or company address
advice: Check shop reviews before buying
Use safe payment methods (e.g. cash on delivery, protected card)
If an offer looks too good, it probably is fake

threats.title: Social-media phishing (Facebook/Messenger)
threats.description: A fake message from a "friend" with a competition link or a login request, used to hijack the account.
warning_signs: An unusual message from a friend, e.g. a competition link
A request for login and password on an external page
A message written in a different style than usual
advice: Do not tap suspicious links, even from friends
Call your friend to verify the message
Enable two-step verification on social accounts

threats.title: Fake antivirus warnings (scareware)
threats.description: A browser pop-up about a "virus" demanding an immediate call to a support number.
warning_signs: An alarming message with sound, blocking the screen
A "support" phone number in the window
Pressure not to close the window and to call now
advice: Close the browser (Alt+F4) or restart the computer
Never call numbers from such pop-ups
A real antivirus never works this way

threats.title: The "Microsoft / Windows support" scam
threats.description: A call or pop-up from an alleged Microsoft employee about a virus, asking for remote access to the computer.
warning_signs: Microsoft never calls on its own initiative
A request to install remote-access software (TeamViewer/AnyDesk)
A demand to pay for a "repair" by card
advice: Hang up — it is always a scam
Never install remote-access programs at a stranger's request
If you already gave access, disconnect from the internet and ask someone for help

threats.title: Fake bank-app update
threats.description: An SMS or e-mail with a link to "update" the bank app, in fact installing malware that intercepts data.
warning_signs: A link to an .apk file or a page outside the app store
A request to install outside Google Play / App Store
An unusual message sender
advice: Update apps only via the official store (Google Play / App Store)
Do not install apps from SMS or e-mail links
If in doubt, ask the bank directly

threats.title: Romance scam
threats.description: A person met online (often posing as someone from abroad) builds an emotional relationship, then asks for money for a "sudden emergency" or travel.
warning_signs: The person never wants to meet in person or on video
Quick declarations of love
Requests for money for various "urgent" needs
advice: Never send money to someone known only online
Talk to family or friends about the new relationship
Check profile photos with image search — they are often stolen

threats.title: Fake crypto / trading platforms
threats.description: An ad promises high, fast investment returns; after depositing, funds are unavailable and "profits" exist only on a fake dashboard.
warning_signs: A promise of very high profits with low risk
Pressure for quick and ever larger deposits
Difficulty or impossibility of withdrawing funds
advice: Do not invest under time pressure or "guaranteed" profit promises
Check whether the firm is supervised by the KNF
Consult family or an independent adviser on every investment

threats.title: Fake "earn from home" job offers
threats.description: An easy remote-job offer requiring an upfront fee for "training" or a "starter pack".
warning_signs: A payment is required before starting work
Very high earnings for minimal effort
No formal employment/contract agreement
advice: A real employer never charges for the chance to work
Check the company in KRS/CEIDG before cooperating
Be wary of offers without a contract

threats.title: Fake refund / overpayment
threats.description: A notice of an alleged overpayment or tax refund, with a link to a form requiring card details.
warning_signs: An unexpected refund requiring card details
A link to a page deceptively similar to gov.pl or a bank
Time pressure ("refund expires in 24h")
advice: Tax refunds never require entering a card number online
Verify by logging in yourself on the official site
Report suspicious messages to CERT Polska (8080)

threats.title: Financial abuse by a carer or relative
threats.description: Someone caring for a close relative — a parent, grandparent, or anyone financially dependent on them (formally or informally) — misuses access to the account, a power of attorney, or payment cards for their own ends.
warning_signs: Sudden, unexplained account changes
The carer isolates that person from other family members
Pressure to sign a power of attorney or will
advice: Keep control of your own documents and login data
Ask another trusted person to look at the finances
If suspicious, contact the bank or social services

threats.title: Pressure to change a will or power of attorney
threats.description: Someone nearby uses psychological pressure so a close relative changes a will, hands over property, or grants power of attorney over an account.
warning_signs: A sudden request to sign important documents "right now"
Isolation from a lawyer or notary independent of the requester
Threats or emotional blackmail
advice: Never sign documents under pressure
Use an independent notary and consult a lawyer
Discuss the decision with a trusted person outside the situation

threats.title: Fake QR codes (quishing)
threats.description: A fake QR sticker (e.g. on a parking meter or advert) leads to a fake payment page or installs malware.
warning_signs: The QR code looks like a sticker placed over existing signage
The scanned page asks for card data
The address after scanning is suspicious or shortened
advice: Check the page address before entering any data
Avoid QR payments in unknown, uncertain places
If in doubt, use the official app, not the QR code

threats.title: Unknown "one ring" calls (Wangiri / ping call)
threats.description: The phone rings once from an unknown, often foreign number; calling back generates high premium-rate charges.
warning_signs: A call from an unknown foreign number, lasting only a moment
The number starts with an unusual country code
Strong curiosity about who called
advice: Do not call back unknown foreign numbers
Check the number online before calling back
Block the number if the calls repeat

threats.title: Fake postal lotteries and competitions
threats.description: A postal letter about winning a lottery you never entered, demanding an "admin fee" to collect the prize.
warning_signs: A lottery win without entering
A payment required to collect the prize
The letter looks official but the sender is unknown or foreign
advice: Real prizes never require upfront payment
Ignore and do not reply to such letters
Consult family if in doubt

threats.title: SIM swap (phone number takeover)
threats.description: A scammer impersonates you to convince your mobile carrier to issue a duplicate SIM card or activate an eSIM on their own device, hijacking the SMS codes your bank uses for authorization.
warning_signs: Sudden, unexplained loss of phone signal
An SMS about a "SIM change" or "eSIM activation" that you never requested
No access to your banking app even though your password is correct
advice: If you suddenly lose signal, contact your carrier another way (e.g. from a different phone)
Ask your carrier to add extra SIM protection (a PIN or a number-porting lock)
Turn on SMS/push notifications in your banking app for every transaction

threats.title: Fake payment link on marketplace apps (OLX/Vinted/Marketplace)
threats.description: A buyer or seller sends a "pay the extra shipping fee" link that closely mimics the real marketplace, used to steal your card details.
warning_signs: The link points outside the marketplace's official domain
Pressure to click quickly before the "offer expires"
The page asks for your full card details, not just an amount
advice: Only pay and receive shipments through the marketplace's own official flow, never a link from a message
Check the exact web address before entering card details
Walk away from the deal if anything feels off

threats.title: Fake toll or parking-fine text messages
threats.description: A text claims you owe an unpaid road toll or parking fine and includes a "pay now" link that leads to a fake payment page.
warning_signs: A shortened link or a domain that looks almost, but not quite, official
Urgency ("pay within 24 hours to avoid a penalty")
A request for card details on a page outside the official payment system
advice: Check any balance only in the official app or website, never through a link from a text
Don't click links in unexpected payment texts
Report the suspicious text to your carrier

threats.title: Fake "easy job" – paid tasks and top-ups
threats.description: A recruiter, usually on Telegram or WhatsApp, offers remote work made of simple "tasks" (likes, reviews), then eventually asks you to pay your own money to "unlock" the earnings you've supposedly made.
warning_signs: The job is offered with no interview and no contract
At some point you're the one asked to pay, in order to get paid
Contact happens only over chat, with no way to verify the company
advice: Never pay your own money to "unlock" earnings
Look the company up in an official business registry before working with them
Cut contact as soon as they ask you to pay anything

threats.title: Faked voice or video (AI deepfake)
threats.description: A scammer uses AI to fake the voice or face of a family member on a video call (a variant of the grandchild scam), or to fake a well-known figure endorsing an investment.
warning_signs: The video or audio feels slightly off (lag, odd expressions)
The caller avoids a longer, natural conversation or hangs up abruptly
A "celebrity" investment endorsement only shows up in an ad, never on that person's own official channels
advice: Verify identity by asking something only the real person would know
Don't trust video or audio of public figures endorsing investments — check their own official channels
If in doubt, end the call and reach that person another, already-known way

threats.title: Rental scam (deposit for a listing that doesn't exist)
threats.description: A fake apartment listing, often priced below market, asks for a deposit before you've seen the place, with the "owner" claiming to be abroad and unable to show it in person.
warning_signs: The price is noticeably below market rate
The "owner" can't show the apartment in person, citing travel abroad
They ask for a deposit by transfer before any lease is signed
advice: Never pay a deposit before viewing the apartment and signing a lease
Check that the person actually has the right to rent out the property
Use established rental platforms and agencies

threats.title: Recruitment as a "money mule"
threats.description: Someone offers easy money for lending your bank account or forwarding transfers you receive — in reality this is money laundering, and the account holder is the one held criminally liable.
warning_signs: An offer of payment for "lending" your bank account or forwarding transfers you receive
A promise of fast, easy money with no explanation of where it comes from
Pressure to open a new account specifically for this
advice: Never let anyone else use your bank account or forward transfers on a stranger's request
Remember that as the account holder, you're the one legally responsible for those transactions
Report the offer to the police

threats.title: Data theft via public Wi-Fi or charging stations
threats.description: Connecting your phone to an unsecured public Wi-Fi network, or to an unknown public USB charging station (so-called "juice jacking"), can let someone intercept your data or install malware.
warning_signs: An open Wi-Fi network with a name that closely mimics an official one (e.g. "Airport_Free")
A public USB charging station with no option to use your own wall charger
Your phone asks you to "trust" an unknown device right after you plug in a cable
advice: Avoid logging into banking apps over unsecured public Wi-Fi
In public places, charge with your own wall adapter or a power bank, not a USB cable plugged into an unknown port
If your phone asks whether to trust a connected device, choose "charge only"
